content:
Sara Li: quick heads up — captured a 90s Nsight timeline on the 16-GPU test that shows weird gaps during the KV merge + all-reduce window. posting screenshots in thread.
Jon Patel: saw that earlier. gaps look like allreduce waiting, but kernels finish early. looks like comm/compute not overlapping.
Vivian Gomez: can you paste the nvtx ranges or share the perf-bot summary?
Sara Li: perf-bot summary below. i also added a tiny custom timer around the KV merge (kv_merge_start/kv_merge_end) and the all-reduce (allred_start/allred_end).
perf-bot: CPU timers: kv_merge 1.2ms, pack/serialize 0.9ms; GPU timers (avg per-GPU): kernel_compute 4.6ms, ncclAllReduce 6.8ms, idle_between 2.1ms. nvprof ranges attached.
Jon Patel: interesting — ncclAllReduce > kernel_compute. but the timeline shows idle slots between compute and nccl ranges on the same stream. might be stream syncs from KV cache refill?
Marco Chen: hypothesis: async kernel launches land on default stream but we have sync points for KV cache writes that force stream ordering. also our kernel selection path sometimes touches host-to-device memcpy for small tensors, which can serialize.
Sara Li: reproducer capture command i used:
```
# Nsight system capture
nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl python -m perf.run_workload --config=tp_pp_16gpu
```
I then dumped nvtx ranges with: `nvtx-range-parser /tmp/run1.qdrep`
Vivian Gomez: did you try setting NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 or enabling NCCL_P2P? could be NCCL progress model issue.
Jon Patel: also try running with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0 (it already is) and move allreduce to separate stream with `cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(stream, cudaStreamNonBlocking)`. need to ensure NCCL calls use that stream.
Marco Chen: small snippet I used to time on-device ops (pseudo):
```
nvtxRangePushA("kv_merge_start");
launch_kv_merge_kernel<<<...>>>(...);
cudaEventRecord(ev1, stream);
nvtxRangePop();
// then nccl allreduce on comm_stream
nvtxRangePushA("allred_start");
ncclAllReduce(..., comm_stream);
cudaEventRecord(ev2, comm_stream);
nvtxRangePop();
```
Measured ev1->ev2 shows 3.9ms gap on some ranks.
Sara Li: I also instrumented per-GPU occupancy and noticed the KV merge kernel is very low occupancy on larger sequence lengths (register pressure from fused kernel). so compute isn't saturating, giving NCCL a chance, but we still see serial behavior.
Vivian Gomez: next experiments: 1) force KV merge to its own nonblocking stream so it doesn't touch default stream ordering 2) run nccl tests with `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS` and `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` forced to isolate network 3) try `CUFFT`-style warmup to prime NVLink? (jk) — more seriously, try increasing NCCL_ASYNC_TESTS and enabling async progress thread.
Jon Patel: please also capture a short `nvprof --profile-api-trace all` on a 2-step run to see if any cudaDeviceSynchronize()s are creeping in (we had one accidental sync in the quantized kernel path last sprint).
Sara Li: agreed. i'll run 3 runs: baseline, KV-merge-on-own-stream, and NCCL async-progress. will attach nsys captures and perf-bot will post summarized timers.
perf-bot: action created: ENG-RUNTIME-482 — Sara to upload captures + perf log by EOD. tagging @Jon Patel @Marco Chen @Vivian Gomez :thumbsup:
Marco Chen: one more note — batching heuristics may cause variable sequence packing which changes kernel shapes and can flip which kernel variant is chosen at kernel-selection time. that can change register usage and trigger these serial gaps. if you can reproduce with deterministic batch layout that will isolate kernel selection effects.
Sara Li: good call. i'll pin batch shapes to fixed sequence lengths for the experiment. thanks all.
Jon Patel: if results look promising, we should try patching comm code to use dedicated comm streams and run the large 48-hour soak. small PR with perf tests first.
Vivian Gomez: if you need help parsing qdrep files i can run the nvtx annotations script.
Sara Li: will do. uploading first capture now.
